They will meter and bill", "rephrased": "Time Warner Cable proposes a distinct solution to internet congestion by implementing a metered billing system that charges customers extra fees for exceeding their data allowances, framing this utility-style model as a fairer alternative to speed throttling.", "summary": "Time Warner Cable proposes metered billing as a fairer alternative to speed throttling."}, "6": {"original": "It is clearly the fairest way to fund the investment that is going to be requi", "rephrased": "Alex Dudley asserts that charging customers directly for the high-speed internet usage they consume is the most equitable method to finance the necessary infrastructure upgrades required to support growing data demands.", "summary": "Alex Dudley asserts that usage-based billing is the fairest way to fund infrastructure."}, "7": {"original": "Art Brodsky of Public Knowledge, a consumer advocacy group in Washington D.C., h", "rephrased": "Art Brodsky of the Washington D.C.-based consumer advocacy group Public Knowledge argues that Time Warner Cable's plan to charge extra fees for excessive data usage functions less as a congestion relief measure and more as a rationing scheme designed to protect inadequate infrastructure from the cable company.", "summary": "Art Brodsky argues Time Warner Cable's plan is a rationing scheme protecting inadequate infrastructure."}}
